question.text: A GOI bond with a coupon rate of 7.50% is trading at Rs. 105.00 in the spot market. The repo rate for financing is 6.50%. What is the approximate net cost of carry for 3 months (simplified)?

explanation.text: The Logic: Net Cost of Carry = Financing Cost on cash price minus Coupon Income. Financing cost for 3 months = 105.00 x 6.50% x (3/12) = Rs. 1.706. Coupon income for 3 months = 100 x 7.50% x (3/12) = Rs. 1.875. Net carry = 1.706 - 1.875 = Rs. -0.169, i.e. approximately Rs. -0.17. The Trap: Rs. 1.625 ignores coupon income altogether. Rs. 0.17 reverses the sign. Rs. -1.625 ignores financing cost. The source-backed formula is financing cost minus coupon income on the cash position, and the negative sign here reflects that coupon income exceeds the financing cost. Note: Corrected the keyed answer from Rs. -0.25 to Rs. -0.17 so it matches the calculation shown in the workbook formula, and removed the cross-exam and pro-tip paragraphs.
